results.why: The display half is already settled — DECISIONS.md rules out over-reporting outright ('starring the feature would hand +2 Stealth to every inventor, including the ten in eleven who chose a different modification'), and the buildable path is fully spec'd. What is left is purely a cost/benefit call the owner has to make and DECISIONS.md explicitly parks on their desk: spend an 11-option picker plus a two-state mode to surface one +2, or leave it in prose. Nothing about the rules decides that.

results.why: Ruling F does not cleanly reach this one. F is about bonuses that BY DEFINITION go to someone else (Aegis for the Innocent targets an ally). Song of Soothing hits 'every creature in the emanation from the creature you hit' and lets you choose whether the target is included — so the wielder genuinely may or may not get it, and the deciding fact is where they are standing, which the app can never know. A permanent star for a bonus you usually will not have, versus no star for one you sometimes will, is a judgement about how much a sheet may over-promise. The answer generalises to every aura/emanation item in the data, so it is worth setting once.

options.label: Display-only mode on the wielder (ruling F clause 2 shape)
options.looksLike: After activating, a 'Song of Soothing (1 min)' pill appears in the rail with the printed text on click. Saves stay unmarked — no number changes. The player reads the pill and applies +1 at the table if they were inside the emanation.

options.label: Star the saves with the positional trigger
options.looksLike: Will/Fort/Ref carry a permanent * whose line reads '+1 status — vs mental effects for 1 minute, only if you were inside your own Song of Soothing's emanation'. Visible whether or not the bow was fired.

options.label: Both: display-only mode AND the star, the star pooled under the mode
options.looksLike: The pill appears on use, and only while it is on do the saves show the *. Costs an appliesWhen modifier on the mode rather than a registry entry.

results.recommend: Option 3, falling back to option 1 if that is more work than it is worth. Ruling E-continued already promises 'every stat a mode affects is highlighted', so gating the star behind the mode is the mechanism the app is heading towards anyway, and it is the only option that never shows a star for a bonus that is not running. Option 2 is the weakest — an always-on star for a once-per-hour, position-dependent bonus is the over-reporting DECISIONS.md rejected for Weapon Innovation.

results.answer: Yes — register the penalty alongside the bonus, as two entries on the same record. The registry already carries 104 negative entries and the cross-cutting stacking ruling says in terms 'this rule for penalties too', so penalties are first-class. Write: [{skill stealth},{skill intimidation}] when "for 1 hour after activating the armor, on Stealth checks and on Intimidation checks to Demoralize" bonus "+2 item"; and [{skill diplomacy},{skill society}] same when, bonus "-2 untyped". Keep the printed penalty UNTYPED — the text names no type, and poolSituationalLines deliberately never pools untyped entries, which is the correct behaviour for an unnamed penalty. Precedent for this exact both-legs-of-one-activation shape: magnetic-suit, earplugs, silvertongue-mutagen.
